sources.title: Perplexity Agent API model reference
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the NVIDIA section identifies Nemotron 3.5 Super and lists the exact perplexity/nemotron-3.5-super-120b-a12b endpoint, with text-only input, reasoning, 1048576 context and 131072 maximum output. The explicit endpoint name carries the published 120B/A12B nominal specification; no exact served checkpoint or tensor inventory is identified.

sources.title: Perplexity API changelog
sources.evidence: An October 2026 entry announces this exact endpoint and repeats its context, output and text-only limits. The entry does not identify a day or served checkpoint.

sources.title: October 19 Perplexity product changelog
sources.evidence: Dated October 19, 2026. Distinguishes Super VL in Search from Super in Agent API and confirms the latter accepts text only. Establishes availability by that date, not the earliest release day. Browser extraction succeeded; direct raw request returned403.

sources.title: Upstream record and identity comments
sources.evidence: Comments identify this record as Perplexity text-only hosting and explicitly say its release day and open-weight flag were borrowed from the separately cataloged NVIDIA VL release. This is provenance of the disputed assertions, not independent technical verification.

sources.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super training recipe
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the architecture diagram labels the language decoder 120B total / 12B active. The specification table independently reports 120B nominal total and 12B per forward pass, distinguishing a 124.453B count including vision encoder, projector and MTP. This supports the nominal language-backbone scope; it does not identify the Perplexity deployment.

sources.title: Separate Super VL BF16 model card
sources.evidence: Official VL checkpoint card documents nominal 120B/12B, hybrid architecture and text/image/video support under OpenMDW-1.1. The current main card was also reopened October 27 and retains these advertised counts. These corroborate the published size designation, but do not establish which checkpoint or auxiliary modules the Perplexity endpoint serves.

sources.title: Super text-only conversion guide
sources.evidence: Describes extracting language and shared MTP weights from a VL checkpoint while omitting media components. It explicitly leaves the public revision unbound and does not mention Perplexity. This demonstrates a possible conversion, not evidence of the hosted endpoint configuration.

sources.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning technical report, October 21 edition
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the October 21 technical report separately publishes 120B total and 12B active for Super. Its released checkpoints are multimodal; its text-only base is also called Super 120B-A12B. The report supplies nominal specifications, but no Perplexity checkpoint binding or exact hosted-service count.

sources.title: Super VL release support article
sources.evidence: The article distinguishes a Super DGX Spark comparison from Super VL in its Figure3 discussion. It supplies no Perplexity checkpoint identity; this reinforces the need to avoid equating names without a binding source.

sources.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning research release
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27: the NVIDIA research release explicitly identifies Nemotron 3.5 Super as nominally 120 billion parameters and 12 billion active. It distinguishes text-only pretraining from multimodal post-training. Targeted NVIDIA and Perplexity searches found no later contradictory size disclosure or exact endpoint checkpoint mapping.

name.note: Preserve the catalog designation for Perplexity’s text-only endpoint. Its explicit 120b-a12b size suffix agrees with NVIDIA’s published nominal specification; it is not an exact tensor measurement.

developer.note: The provider attributes the model to NVIDIA; Perplexity is the host.

family.note: Named Nemotron 3.5 Super by the host; retain the existing family key.

release_date.note: Primary API changelog establishes October2026; public product changelog establishes availability by October19. The baseline October15 day was borrowed from the separate VL launch and is not verified for this endpoint.

open_weights.note: The exact hosted checkpoint is unidentified. Public VL weights and a text-only conversion recipe do not establish that this endpoint’s weights are publicly released; do not claim either open or closed.

license.note: No governing model-weight license is identified for this exact endpoint. OpenMDW-1.1 belongs to the accessible VL checkpoint; a provider binding would be needed to apply it here.

parameters_b.note: Retain 120B as the published nominal language-backbone size for the hosted offer: Perplexity explicitly names NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super and uses 120b-a12b in this exact endpoint, while NVIDIA independently publishes 120B and scopes that number to its decoder. Exact hosted checkpoint and loaded auxiliary components remain unknown. Do not substitute the separate VL complete-checkpoint count or present 120B as a measured service inventory.

active_parameters_b.note: Retain independently published nominal 12B active parameters for the language backbone, supported by NVIDIA’s per-forward-pass specification and decoder diagram and by the exact hosted endpoint’s A12B designation. This is not derived by equating active and total parameters. It does not assert an exact hosted per-token tensor count, MTP contribution or media-processing cost.

architecture.note: Perplexity explicitly identifies its named 120B-A12B offer as NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super. NVIDIA documents that model's language backbone as hybrid Mamba-Transformer LatentMoE. This establishes the published coarse model architecture, without claiming an identical hosted checkpoint or auxiliary-module inventory.

context_window.note: Exact provider-documented context limit;131072 is a separate output limit.

modalities.note: Text-only endpoint, preserved separately from Super VL. Provider documents generated text and no media inputs for this identifier.

reasoning.note: The provider explicitly identifies this endpoint as a reasoning model.

tool_call.note: Baseline support was inferred from the Nemotron family. The exact model documentation confirms reasoning but not custom function calling, and warns that generic Agent API tools are not supported by every model. No authenticated capability test was performed.

description.value: NVIDIA reasoning model served through Perplexity’s Agent API with text-only input and a 1,048,576-token context window.
description.note: Describes the documented hosted offering without asserting exact tensor counts or VL capabilities.

patch.description: NVIDIA reasoning model served through Perplexity’s Agent API with text-only input and a 1,048,576-token context window.
patch.notes: Perplexity’s text-only perplexity/nemotron-3.5-super-120b-a12b offer names NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super. Retain the published nominal language-backbone specification of 120B total and 12B active, supported by the exact endpoint designation and NVIDIA’s separate total/active disclosures and decoder scope. These rounded specifications are not an exact inventory of the hosted service. The served checkpoint and auxiliary modules remain unidentified; the separate VL complete-checkpoint count is not applied here. The published hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE architecture follows the same model identity. Weight availability, model license and custom-tool support retain their prior unverified assessments. Primary sources establish October 2026 availability without a verified release day; context and reasoning are explicitly documented.

identity_review.census: Not performed for the endpoint: no bound checkpoint was identified. Downloaded only candidate VL metadata, configuration, code and card for identity review; no tensor payloads or headers were attributed to this endpoint.
identity_review.access_limits: Unauthenticated Perplexity /v1/models returned401. Non-VL guessed HF repositories returned401, which does not prove nonexistence. The old NVIDIA Build route returned genericHTML but its Markdown card returned404. Public provider documentation was accessible.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: restore verified nominal 120B total and 12B active for the named offer’s language backbone. Reopened Perplexity’s exact endpoint documentation, its October 19 announcement, NVIDIA’s training recipe, current VL card, text-only conversion guide and October 21 report; also checked the research release and searched for missed or later disclosures. NVIDIA’s decoder scope resolves the nominal-count question without requiring an exact hosted tensor census. Exact checkpoint and auxiliary-module composition remain unresolved. Other audited values are unchanged. The same named-model evidence also supports the coupled hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE architecture correction.
